title: STUDY TOPIC JESUS AND THE SPIRIT. Part 8
devotional:
The Baptism Of Jesus. Matthew 3:13-16

Many people, both Christians and non Christians are living with an acute crisis of identity. Sadly too many Christians do not know who they are.

‘Most Christians do not know who they are in Christ, to one degree of another. We all wear false labels or identities which can lead to a lot of confusion, loneliness, anxiety, failure, insecurity, depression, and fear, with a ripple effect that goes into our families and all interpersonal areas of our lives. Add to that, once Satan can take the child of God down in the area of our image, he wins, as we become isolated, depressed, ineffectual in life, and ultimately hopeless that we'll never change, or our circumstances will never change.’ Penny Wiser White. Who Am I?

Knowing who we are before God is essential for a holy and effective life. Many of our insecurities and fears stem from our confusion and uncertainty about our identity. So we look for an identity in all the wrong places not realising that in doing this we are actually affirming and enabling our insecurities. People go into old age addicted to their insecurities because they have spent their whole life finding their identity in the wrong place. There is a danger that we become so wrapped up in what we are doing for God that we neglect our relationship with Him. If what we achieve or do for God becomes more important than our relationship with Him, we are creating a false identity which can become all about us and how good we are and how God should be thankful that we’re on His side. Now, we’re never going to say that, but perhaps this is what Jesus was talking about in Matthew 7 when He said theses words: - ‘Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name and in your name drive out demons and in your name perform many miracles?’ ‘Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you. Away from me, you evildoers!’ Matthew 7;22-23 Obviously God knows everyone, but what Jesus was saying here was, I didn’t know you intimately. I knew what you were doing, that was plain for all to see, but I didn’t know your heart.

As we are going to see from the life of Jesus, the role of the Holy Spirit in our lives is to help us accept that we are children of God.

Paul said it this way in Romans 8:15-16 ‘’So you have not received a spirit that makes you fearful slaves. Instead, you received God’s Spirit when he adopted you as his own children. Now we call him, “Abba, Father. For his Spirit joins with our spirit to affirm that we are God’s children.’’

We need to get our minds around this. As it was for Jesus so it needs to be for us. The primary work of the Spirit is to help us find our identity in the Father’s love. I do not hear many people pray about this. We are happy to rightly ask the Spirit to help us in our ministry, or to work in the lives of others, but rarely do we seek the Spirit’s help when it comes to discovering and accepting who we are. And yet identity rooted in the love of the Father, through the work of the Spirit, needs to be the place from where our lives and ministry come from.

We know that Jesus did his ministry through the power of the Spirit, see Acts 10:38 & Luke 4:18.

But this power of the Spirit for ministry was an expression of him knowing his Fathers love. He did what he did in ministry not only because he knew that his father loved Him, but because he also knew that the father loves us.

‘’There was no identity crisis in the life of Jesus Christ. He knew who He was. He knew where He had come from, and why he was here. And he knew where He was going. And when you are that liberated, then you can serve.’’ Howard Hendricks. Howard G. Hendricks quotefancy.com. Accessed 3/04/2025

The Holy Spirit at the Baptism of Jesus

1. Let’s consider the heart attitude as Jesus got baptised.

a. Humility.

Jesus went to John to be baptized. This is very strange because John was baptizing people because they were turning from their sin and turning to God. See Matthew 3:1-12.

We know that Jesus had lived a life free from sin, he lived a life in continual fellowship with his Father, so why did he want John to baptize him? He chose to be baptized so he could humbly identify with us. His baptism was an expression of profound humility and radical identification. You could say that in some ways the humility and identification that Jesus expressed in his baptism was a shadow of the humility and identification he would show at the cross. Jesus would be unable to accomplish his father’s will without living a life of continual humility. His humility enabled him to meaningfully relate to every broken and needy person he met.

b. Prayer.

Luke tells us, ‘As he was praying the heavens opened.’ we do not know what Jesus prayed for, but there may be a clue in the text.

Isaiah 64:1-4

‘Oh, that you would rend the heavens and come down, that the mountains would tremble before you! 2 As when fire sets twigs ablaze and causes water to boil, come down to make your name known to your enemies and cause the nations to quake before you! 3 or when you did awesome things that we did not expect, you came down, and the mountains trembled before you. 4 Since ancient times no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who acts on behalf of those who wait for him.’

It is interesting to note that the prayer recorded in Isaiah 64:1-4 is that God would rend the heavens, come down and make His name known to His enemies by great displays of power causing the mountains to tremble. However, when God tore open the heavens, his power and glory were not displayed in the way the prayer in Isaiah had hoped or expected. There was no powerful display of God’s just wrath, but a display of the tender love of a father. At the beginning of Jesus’ ministry, He needed to be reminded of His Fathers unconditional love and acceptance, He was His fathers son.
prayer: Father please help me to know that my identity is in you, not in the work that I do.
